subject: Deadline drift: orchestration, risk register, and escalation
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healthmetrics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Park <david.park@healthmetrics.com>
Date: 2026-09-24T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Concern: acceptance window slipping week of Oct 4

Vanessa / Marcus,

Quick note from Procurement / Program Management: due to an internal QA hold, our acceptance window is at risk of slipping by ~7 business days which will push the cutover outside of our originally planned Oct 12 go-live. I know we already have a MAP in place, but wanted to surface the impact so we can align on a mitigations list and whether an official rebaseline is needed.

Immediate questions:
- Can Redwood commit to an accelerated canary slot the week of Oct 5 if we push the final acceptance?
- What are the minimal deliverables you need from us to keep the eval moving?

I attached the latest MAP (v2) and our internal timeline note. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Senior Program Manager
HealthMetrics Inc.

Attachments: healthmetrics_MAP_v2.pdf, internal_timeline_note.txt

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healthmetrics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Park <david.park@healthmetrics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-25T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Concern: acceptance window slipping week of Oct 4

Thanks for flagging this, Samantha — appreciate the early warning. Quick read of the MAP confirms there are three dependent items on your side (QA sign-off, test dataset handoff, and a final procurement approval). From Redwood's perspective we have two levers:

1) Fast-track a canary (we can provision a limited canary on Oct 5-6) — needs a minimal test dataset and pre-authorized access.
2) Shift the acceptance gates in the MAP with a one-week rebaseline and add a contingency weekend for cutover.

Action items for HealthMetrics (please):
- Share the sanitized test dataset by EOD Tue (9/28)
- Confirm whether procurement can issue the final PO hold by 9/29

Marcus — I asked Priyom to join this thread because he'll own the risk register and formal escalation if we need an exec exception for credits or SLA windowing. If we can't secure the dataset by 9/28 we'll need to propose the rebaseline formally to execs and outline the mitigation commitments.

I'll draft a short mitigation plan and proposed MAP change and circulate for sign-off.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0124

Attachments referenced: none in this message

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healthmetrics.com>, David Park <david.park@healthmetrics.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Risk register: current exposures and proposed mitigations

Vanessa / Priyom / Samantha — attaching the initial risk register (close_risk_register_2026-09.xlsx). Summary below:

Current exposures:
- R1: QA hold (external) => Likely 5-8 business day delay unless dataset provided.
- R2: Procurement approval flighting => PO authorization currently pending, 2-4 day uncertainty window.
- R3: Canary capacity contention => Redwood can support limited canary but needs KV caching prewarm and 2 engineer hours for runbook testing.

Proposed mitigations (short form):
- If dataset arrives by 9/28: proceed with Oct 5 canary.
- If dataset slips to 9/30: schedule canary as Oct 7 and negotiate a cutover weekend to Oct 15-16.
- If procurement does not issue PO by 9/29: request procurement hold extension and escalate to procurement execs for approval.

Priyom, please advise if we should elevate this to the Customer Success Director for an SLA credit consideration. Vanessa — I recommend we prepare a one-page exec memo outlining the tradeoffs (map changes, potential credits, and operational commitments) and request a 48-hour review from HealthMetrics.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: close_risk_register_2026-09.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@healthmetrics.com>, David Park <david.park@healthmetrics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deadline drift: orchestration, risk register, and escalation

Samantha / David — per internal review and Marcus's register, here's a concise set of asks and next steps so we don't lose runway:

1) HealthMetrics deliverables (by 9/30 EOD):
   - Sanitized test dataset (minimum slice for canary) — healthmetrics to upload to shared drive link in this thread.
   - Confirmation on PO timing (Procurement) or contact for escalation.

2) Redwood commitments:
   - We will provision a limited canary environment Oct 5-6 if dataset is received on 9/30 morning and procurement confirms access.
   - If dataset misses 9/30, propose formal rebaseline: new acceptance target Oct 20 with a Oct 15-16 weekend cutover contingency.
   - If rebaseline is accepted, Redwood will commit 3 engineer-days for canary prep and two weekend support engineers at no additional cost (subject to exec approval).

3) Escalation ask (from HealthMetrics): if procurement cannot confirm PO by 9/29, please provide the procurement exec contact and we will escalate. If HealthMetrics prefers Redwood to request an SLA exception/credit, we will prepare the one-page memo for sign-off.

Samantha — can you confirm by EOD today whether the dataset will be delivered and whether procurement has an exec contact? If not, we'll prepare the rebaseline proposal and cc our CS Director for credit discussion.

Thanks — I'll draft the MAP amendment and share a short exec memo if escalation is required.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: healthmetrics_MAP_v2.pdf (referenced), close_risk_register_2026-09.xlsx (attached earlier)
